source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON), WHO AFRO situation reports, and Africa CDC bulletins reporting Mpox cases and deaths in DRC for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO DON and Africa CDC are the highest-priority primary reporting channels for DRC Mpox during the August 2024 outbreak escalation period. These sources contain extractable confirmed, probable, suspected case counts and deaths at national and subnational level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify DRC Ministry of Health (Ministère de la Santé Publique) and INRB epidemiological bulletins (bulletins épidémiologiques) for Mpox in DRC covering August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: The DRC MoH and INRB are the national authoritative sources for subnational (province and health zone) Mpox surveillance data. French-language bulletins are the primary format and are essential for subnational_location and locality field extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Mpox situation reports and multi-country updates covering DRC for the period 2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO global Mpox sitreps published in August 2024 aggregate DRC-specific data and may include subnational breakdowns, clade I/Ib distinctions, and weekly case/death counts extractable for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (Global.health, Our World in Data, ProMED) that aggregate DRC Mpox case and death counts for August 2024 for cross-validation.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide independently aggregated counts that can be held back and used to validate extracted records from primary collection sources without leakage.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ECDC rapid risk assessments or technical reports covering DRC Mpox clade I/Ib for August 2024 as a secondary validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: ECDC published technical assessments on DRC Mpox clade Ib in mid-2024 that include epidemiological summaries usable for validation of case and death counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature and preprints describing DRC Mpox clade I/Ib epidemiology, case definitions, and surveillance methodology for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources clarify case definitions (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), clade classification, and count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly) needed to correctly interpret and normalize extracted records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify news and situation report sources (Reuters, AP, Reliefweb, OCHA) covering DRC Mpox outbreak in August 2024 for early signal detection and subnational location corroboration.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and humanitarian situation reports may contain early outbreak signals, subnational location names, and corroborating counts that support collection and help identify gaps in official reporting.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. incident), unclear reporting periods, or mixed clade data for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: DRC Mpox reporting in August 2024 involved both clade I and clade Ib, cumulative and weekly counts, and national vs. subnational aggregations. Sources that do not clearly distinguish these dimensions require human adjudication.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: WHO AFRO, WHO HQ Disease Outbreak News, Africa CDC, DRC Ministry of Health (Ministère de la Santé Publique, Hygiène et Prévention), and INRB (Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale) are the authoritative primary reporting agencies for DRC Mpox. These sources publish weekly and monthly epidemiological bulletins with subnational (province, health zone) case and death breakdowns, confirmed/probable/suspected case classifications, and clade I/Ib distinctions directly relevant to the August 2024 target window.

WHO global Mpox situation reports, ECDC rapid risk assessments, OCHA humanitarian situation reports, and Reliefweb updates provide independently compiled DRC Mpox data for August 2024. These serve as validation sources because they aggregate data from official DRC sources but are published independently, enabling cross-check of case and death counts.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints (PubMed, medRxiv, Lancet, NEJM, Eurosurveillance) on DRC Mpox clade I/Ib epidemiology published in 2024 provide case definitions, surveillance methodology context, and may contain extractable case/death data for the August 2024 period. Essential for interpreting count semantics and normalizing confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classifications.

Structured public-health databases including Global.health line lists, Our World in Data Mpox tracker, WHO Mpox data repository, and ProMED archive provide machine-readable or structured DRC Mpox counts for August 2024. These are held back for validation to cross-check extracted records from primary collection sources.

Reputable news outlets (Reuters, AP, AFP, BBC), humanitarian portals (Reliefweb, OCHA), and health news aggregators (CIDRAP, Health Policy Watch) published DRC Mpox outbreak coverage in August 2024 coinciding with the WHO PHEIC declaration. These sources provide early outbreak signals, subnational location corroboration, and may cite official figures directly quotable as evidence.
